mitigation_mechanism: In-field practices let more rain infiltrate and hold water in the soil, so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï pits gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year on degraded land that otherwise yielded nothing, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. The zaï and stone-bund yield figures come from one study, Kaboré and Reij, the stone-bund figure as restated by Zougmoré and colleagues, so they are not independent confirmations [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. In Malawi's El Niño drought season ground cover (a soil-cover mulch, modelled separately from the other practices) raised maize from 247 kg per hectare on control plots to 432 kg per hectare and raised the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement [ev_crop_yield_boil19_2, ev_food_security_boil19_1]. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers obtained 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 368 kg on conventional plots in the 2006/07 season, which the source calls a drought year [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 2.53 against 1.82 t per hectare without inputs (not significant) and 4.10 against 3.15 t per hectare with manure and fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3]. Storage works carry water into dry periods: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, Indian farmers reported a 6% chance of crop failure from aberrant rains with a farm pond against 20% without, cisterns on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and WOCAT compilers for a pond in Cambodia and check dams in Somalia rate drought impacts as reduced, the Cambodian sheet noting the pond provides enough water even during drought and the Somali sheet crediting improved soil moisture retention and infiltration [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. The Vallerani-system compiler in Burkina Faso credits water storage in the soil profile, and the Uzbek orchard-terrace compiler notes that more water is captured and infiltrated [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts]. Sand dams carry water into drought years: in Zimbabwe the months water could be collected at sand-dam sites in a drought year rose from 5.8 before construction to 9.7 after, and in a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the contrast was 1520 against 400 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_2]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the dry spells of the season [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm and 1-m half-moon plots mitigated the impact of dry spells by retaining moisture for 2-3 weeks [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. In on-farm conservation-farming trials in Kenya, Tanzania and Ethiopia the largest yield difference over conventional ploughing came in rainy seasons with low rainfall, when the practice maximises rainfall infiltration so the crop can bridge short periods of dry spell [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. In Zambia's 2001/2 season of very scattered rainfall, maize in hand-hoe conservation-farming basins yielded 3,054 kg per hectare against 1,339 kg under ploughing, which the authors say showcased the water-harvesting benefits of the basins [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1]. Farmers practising basins in Zambia, Zimbabwe and Limpopo reported maize and sorghum yields of >1 tonnes per hectare even in seasons with poor rainfall (<450 mm), against total crop failure under conventional ploughing [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. In a Zimbabwe household panel, conservation agriculture (mostly planting basins, with residue mulch and rotation on some plots) improved maize yields during times of drought, and sorghum and cowpea yields too [ev_crop_yield_mich19_3, ev_crop_yield_mich19_5]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths, as easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. In a Burkina Faso farm-pond trial, sorghum given supplemental irrigation from the harvested runoff yielded 680 against 443 kg per hectare in 1999 and 1138 against 634 kg per hectare in 2000, both seasons with serious dry spells [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_4, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_5]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial (Barron and Okwach), supplemental irrigation from a runoff-fed earth dam plus fertiliser raised maize yields over fertilised plots without irrigation in low-rainfall seasons (<300 mm) but not in seasons above 300 mm, and in a dry long-rains season only the irrigated plots produced any grain at all [ev_crop_yield_barr05_3, ev_crop_yield_barr05_4]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia (Bouma and colleagues) found significantly larger yield improvements in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter years, and gains in below-average rainfall years that were higher but not significant [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. In semi-arid north-east Nigeria, tied ridging with a wood-shavings mulch raised sorghum grain yield by 67% over a flat bed in 1999, a season that ended in drought at grain filling [ev_crop_yield_chir06_6]. In southern Malawi's 2015/16 El Niño season, maize hybrids under conservation agriculture (planting in small holes with residue cover) yielded 700 kg per hectare more on average than under conventional ridge tillage [ev_crop_yield_seti18_1]. A terracing study citing De Graaff (2005) states that terracing reduces the risk of crop failure during dry spells in the rainy season through its water-conserving effect [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13]. In Ethiopia, the Sustainable Land Management Programme reduced vulnerability to severe drought in treated watersheds against control watersheds, with programme effects three times larger where severe droughts occurred, and buffered moderate droughts significantly on both vegetation measures used [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2]. A risk model of a Burkina Faso farm reservoir, built on field experience, finds all mild dry spells mitigated by supplemental irrigation and severe late dry spells reduced to mild ones [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_7, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. A watershed model of the Arvari in Rajasthan (Glendenning and Vervoort 2011, cited in a review) found rainwater harvesting gave a slight buffer in drought years through more reliable groundwater stores, despite reducing streamflow [ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6]. A survey and modelling study in semi-arid Zimbabwe (Kahinda et al. 2007, cited in a review) found rainwater irrigation from macro-catchments raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre by mitigating intra-seasonal dry spells [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5].
caveats: The benefit shrinks or vanishes in severe drought: stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year (1985), Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, zaï only buffers a dry spell of two to three weeks where soil water storage is sufficient, and in Mozambique no cowpea yield was obtained on any treatment in a season heavily affected by drought [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_2]. In the Kenyan trial's short rains with meteorological droughts, tied ridging gave no advantage (0.52 against 0.53 t per hectare without inputs, 1.17 against 1.27 with manure and fertiliser) because there was little or no rainwater to hold in the basins [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5, ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]. A water-harvesting review states that dry spells can be bridged through water management but crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought [ev_crop_yield_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Storage also runs out, with subsurface dams in Brazil drying out in a rainless year and consecutive drought years in Tunisia limiting soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. The pool includes on-farm or trial measurements from Malawi, Kenya, Zimbabwe and Mozambique, alongside WOCAT compiler ratings and institutional assertions; the Zimbabwe planting-basin gain also carries manure and fertiliser, the Indian pond figures come from a preprint farmer survey, the sand-dam figures rest on recall interviews, and the Rwandan and Ethiopian programme results come from bundled programmes [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4]. Not every in-field practice helped in that Malawi El Nino season: banking, the reinforcement of ridges while the crop is growing, cut maize from 245 to 153 kg per hectare and lowered the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054 [ev_crop_yield_boil19_5, ev_food_security_boil19_3]. The Ethiopian dry-spell finding is a field observation of which plots wilted, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. The Burkina Faso half-moon and zaï moisture finding is the authors' statement about dry spells, for pits filled with compost [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. Water harvesting is not irrigation, and the new primaries mark the limit: at the more arid Kenyan sites of Laikipia and Machakos each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, with 0 kg per hectare of maize harvested at Machakos due to meteorological drought, and the conservation-farming treatments did not avert it [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. In the Zimbabwe panel conservation agriculture had no specific impact in mitigating rainfall-shortfall losses for millet and groundnut [ev_crop_yield_mich19_6]. The East African low-rainfall gain is for the best system per site, ripping or pitting usually with fertiliser, so it is bundled with reduced tillage and fertiliser, and the authors read it as a trend from their own figure [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. The Zambia 2001/2 basin contrast is a raw comparison in a single season with no normal-year reference, and most basin farmers received hybrid seed, fertiliser and lime on credit, so part of the gap is the input package [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1]. The farmer-reported basin yields compare fertilised basins with unfertilised ploughing, which the author warns makes those datasets too confounded [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. The Zimbabwe panel's drought-season gains are interaction estimates for conservation agriculture as practised (planting basins bundled with residue mulch and rotation); its normal-season results are reported in the production row, not here [ev_crop_yield_mich19_3, ev_crop_yield_mich19_5]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. In the Kenyan dam trial's drought season the catchment yielded no runoff to irrigate with, both biomass and grain were strongly hit by the lack of water, and no treatment differed from another [ev_crop_yield_barr05_5]. The Burkina Faso reservoir model marks the limit: a meteorological drought cannot be mitigated because there is too little water to harvest, and severe late dry spells at flowering and grain filling are only partly mitigated because the reservoir supports two supplemental irrigations where at least three are needed [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_5, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. The Ethiopian programme result is measured on remotely sensed vegetation greenness and productivity rather than crop yields, comes from a programme that bundles surface water harvesting with small-scale irrigation, gully rehabilitation, grazing control and reforestation, and under mild drought the buffering showed on the greenness index but not on the productivity measure [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4].

justification.statement: water_harvesting_conservation moderately reduces the impact of drought in BFA, BRA, CHN, ECU, ETH, GHA, IND, JPN, KEN, KHM, KOR, MOZ, MWI, NER, NGA, PAK, PER, RWA, SOM, TUN, TZA, UZB, ZAF, ZMB, ZWE; the measured evidence also includes no-benefit or reversal results under drought, which discount the class; measured HARM (maladaptation) in 2 sources — the practice worsened this outcome for some adopters (robust evidence, high agreement → very_high confidence; transfer: in_context). Part of this effect is off-site (downstream or landscape scale) rather than on the adopting farm.

justification.conditionality: The benefit shrinks or vanishes in severe drought: stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year (1985), Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, zaï only buffers a dry spell of two to three weeks where soil water storage is sufficient, and in Mozambique no cowpea yield was obtained on any treatment in a season heavily affected by drought [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_2]. Not every in-field practice helped in that Malawi El Nino season: banking, the reinforcement of ridges while the crop is growing, cut maize from 245 to 153 kg per hectare and lowered the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054 [ev_crop_yield_boil19_5, ev_food_security_boil19_3]. The Burkina Faso half-moon and zaï moisture finding is the authors' statement about dry spells, for pits filled with compost [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. Water harvesting is not irrigation, and the new primaries mark the limit: at the more arid Kenyan sites of Laikipia and Machakos each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, with 0 kg per hectare of maize harvested at Machakos due to meteorological drought, and the conservation-farming treatments did not avert it [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. mitigation_mechanism: In upper-middle-income semi-arid settings the evidence is mostly from Brazil, where water from runoff ponds used as supplemental irrigation has reduced crop-loss risk in years of irregular rainfall and production-cistern water for livestock can reduce animal deaths in the most severe droughts [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths, as easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies from countries including China, India, Ethiopia, Kenya and South Africa found yield improvements significantly higher in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter years, and yield gains, though not significant, in below-average rainfall years [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. Terracing is also cited as reducing the risk of crop failure during dry spells in the rainy season (De Graaff, 2005, cited by Adgo et al.) [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13].
caveats: Storage runs short in prolonged drought: Brazilian subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small manually built ones do not withstand long dry spells, which records no benefit rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The meta-analysis compares rainfall classes across studies and states no drought-year size, and the terracing statement is a second-hand citation without a measurement, so the row records the direction only [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13].

mitigation_mechanism: These are programme-scale or unspecified soil and water conservation packages. In Ethiopia's Sustainable Land Management Project, whose measures include surface water-harvesting systems, a satellite difference-in-differences comparison of treated and control watersheds found that the programme reduced vulnerability to severe drought, with effects in areas that had severe droughts three times larger than the average programme effect (increases of 16.71% in EVI and 13.48% in GOSIF-GPP), and significant buffering under moderate drought [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies found significantly higher yield improvements in years with rainfall below 330 mm [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. A review of impact studies finds such methods particularly useful in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability, Ethiopia's PSNP public works improved watershed drought resilience by increasing water availability, and in semi-arid Brazil production cisterns can reduce animal mortality in severe drought [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. Physical soil and water conservation structures were also reported to buffer crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia, and a water-harvesting review states that dry spells can be bridged through investments in water management [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm and 1-m half-moon plots mitigated the impact of dry spells by retaining moisture for 2-3 weeks, and a Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].
caveats: The buffering weakens at the mild end and fails at the extreme end. Under mild drought the Ethiopian programme's EVI model still detects a small significant effect but the GOSIF-GPP model shows none [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4]. A water-harvesting review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought and different coping mechanisms are required [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. The PSNP note adds that vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years (the measured harm in this row), and in Tunisia four consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. Almost every unit is a bundled programme, pooled soil and water conservation or an expert review, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated: water harvesting is one of several listed Ethiopian programme measures, and many meta-analysis observations also carried soil fertility treatment [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. The Brazilian statement describes potential without data, the Ethiopian 2015 finding is a secondary citation, the Burkina Faso moisture finding is for pits filled with compost, and the Burkina Faso review conclusion has no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].

justification.mechanism: Zaï and tassa pits increase infiltration and the water retention capacity of the soil, so crops suffer less from drought spells at the onset of and during the rainy season [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In rainfall-deficit periods zaï allowed cereals to be grown on degraded crusted soils in Burkina Faso, gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year where untreated land yielded nothing, and only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger [ev_crop_yield_roose93_3, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s]. In Malawi's El Niño drought season ground cover (a soil-cover mulch, modelled separately from the other practices) raised maize from 247 kg per hectare on control plots to 432 kg per hectare and raised the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement [ev_crop_yield_boil19_2, ev_food_security_boil19_1]. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers obtained 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 368 kg on conventional plots in the 2006/07 season, which the source calls a drought year [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 2.53 against 1.82 t per hectare without inputs (not significant) and 4.10 against 3.15 t per hectare with manure and fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3]. Chololo pits in Tanzania are reported to mitigate drought effects [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_7]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the contrast was 1520 against 400 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_2]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the dry spells of the season [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. In on-farm conservation-farming trials in Kenya, Tanzania and Ethiopia the largest yield difference over conventional ploughing came in rainy seasons with low rainfall, when the practice maximises rainfall infiltration so the crop can bridge short periods of dry spell [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. In Zambia's 2001/2 season of very scattered rainfall, maize in hand-hoe conservation-farming basins yielded 3,054 kg per hectare against 1,339 kg under ploughing, which the authors say showcased the water-harvesting benefits of the basins [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1]. Farmers practising basins in Zambia, Zimbabwe and Limpopo reported maize and sorghum yields of >1 tonnes per hectare even in seasons with poor rainfall (<450 mm), against total crop failure under conventional ploughing [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. In a Zimbabwe household panel, conservation agriculture (mostly planting basins, with residue mulch and rotation on some plots) improved maize yields during times of drought, and sorghum and cowpea yields too [ev_crop_yield_mich19_3, ev_crop_yield_mich19_5]. In semi-arid north-east Nigeria, tied ridging with a wood-shavings mulch raised sorghum grain yield by 67% over a flat bed in 1999, a season that ended in drought at grain filling [ev_crop_yield_chir06_6]. In southern Malawi's 2015/16 El Niño season, maize hybrids under conservation agriculture (planting in small holes with residue cover) yielded 700 kg per hectare more on average than under conventional ridge tillage [ev_crop_yield_seti18_1].
justification.conditionality: Zaï only reduces the impact of a dry spell of two to three weeks, and only where soil water storage capacity is at least 50 mm [ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In the Kenyan trial's short rains with meteorological droughts, tied ridging gave no advantage (0.52 against 0.53 t per hectare without inputs, 1.17 against 1.27 with manure and fertiliser) because there was little or no rainwater to hold in the basins [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5, ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]. In Mozambique no cowpea yield was obtained on any treatment in a season heavily affected by drought [ev_crop_yield_thierf15_2]. The family rests partly on on-farm or trial measurements in Malawi, Kenya, Zimbabwe and Mozambique; the zaï and tassa contrasts are author estimates, the Zimbabwe planting-basin gain also carries manure and fertiliser, and the Kenyan tied-ridging result is a single-site trial [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1]. Not every in-field practice helped in that Malawi El Nino season: banking, the reinforcement of ridges while the crop is growing, cut maize from 245 to 153 kg per hectare and lowered the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054 [ev_crop_yield_boil19_5, ev_food_security_boil19_3]. The Ethiopian dry-spell finding is a field observation of which plots wilted, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. Water harvesting is not irrigation, and the new primaries mark the limit: at the more arid Kenyan sites of Laikipia and Machakos each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, with 0 kg per hectare of maize harvested at Machakos due to meteorological drought, and the conservation-farming treatments did not avert it [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. In the Zimbabwe panel conservation agriculture had no specific impact in mitigating rainfall-shortfall losses for millet and groundnut [ev_crop_yield_mich19_6]. The East African low-rainfall gain is for the best system per site, ripping or pitting usually with fertiliser, so it is bundled with reduced tillage and fertiliser, and the authors read it as a trend from their own figure [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. The Zambia 2001/2 basin contrast is a raw comparison in a single season with no normal-year reference, and most basin farmers received hybrid seed, fertiliser and lime on credit, so part of the gap is the input package [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1]. The farmer-reported basin yields compare fertilised basins with unfertilised ploughing, which the author warns makes those datasets too confounded [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. The Zimbabwe panel's drought-season gains are interaction estimates for conservation agriculture as practised (planting basins bundled with residue mulch and rotation); its normal-season results are reported in the production row, not here [ev_crop_yield_mich19_3, ev_crop_yield_mich19_5].

mitigation_mechanism: Runoff stored in a farm pond and applied as supplemental irrigation carries crops through dry spells. In a Kenyan on-farm trial, supplemental irrigation from a lined earth dam fed by surface runoff, with fertilizer, raised maize yields over fertilised non-irrigated plots in seasons below 300 mm of rain, and in the LR00 drought season only the irrigated plots yielded grain at all [ev_crop_yield_barr05_3, ev_crop_yield_barr05_4]. In a Burkina Faso randomised trial with a hand-dug farm pond, irrigated sorghum yielded 680 against 443 kg per ha in 1999 and 1138 against 634 kg per ha in 2000 [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_4, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_5]; the companion risk analysis finds all mild dry spells mitigated and severe late-season dry spells only partly mitigated, turned into mild stress [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_7, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. Pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns catching runoff on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and a review of small reservoirs counts improved drought resilience among their cited benefits [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1]. WOCAT compilers in Cambodia and Somalia rate drought impacts as reduced [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. A water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, and rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss in critical drought periods [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2]. Biazin et al. cite Kahinda et al. (2007) in semi-arid Zimbabwe for rainwater irrigation from macro-catchments raising water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per m3 by mitigating intra-seasonal dry spells [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5]. Indian farmers reported a 6% chance of rainy-season crop failure from aberrant rains with a farm pond against 20% without one, and Glendenning et al. cite Glendenning and Vervoort (2011), a Rajasthan watershed model in which rainwater harvesting gave a slight buffer in drought years through more reliable groundwater stores [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6]. Sand dams extend supply into drought: in Zimbabwe the months water could be collected at sand-dam sites in a drought year rose from 5.8 before construction to 9.7 after, and in a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins, as easing the effects of droughts on lowland crops [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8].
caveats: There has to be runoff to store. In the Kenyan SR98 season the dam barely filled, so there was no harvested runoff for irrigation and no treatment differed in yield; the Burkina Faso risk analysis puts the probability of drought at 0.1 and finds it cannot be mitigated because there is too little water to harvest, and the reservoir supports only two irrigation applications where a severe late dry spell needs at least three [ev_crop_yield_barr05_5, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_5, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. Brazilian subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long droughts [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. So the strong effect is a dry-spell effect within a season that still produces runoff, not a defence against a failed season. The Kenyan and Burkina Faso trial gains also depend on fertilizer: in the Kenyan high-rainfall seasons above 300 mm irrigation added no yield, and in Burkina Faso nutrients were the primary limiting factor [ev_crop_yield_barr05_3, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_5]. These trials apply stored water as supplemental irrigation, at the boundary between water harvesting and irrigation. The Loess Plateau claim is a qualitative assertion, the reservoir finding a vote count, the Brazilian pond and barraginha statements institutional assertions without data, and the WOCAT units compiler ratings [ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The supplemental-irrigation, crop-loss, Zimbabwe water-productivity and Rajasthan findings are secondary citations in reviews, the Indian pond figures come from a farmer survey reported in a preprint, and the sand-dam results rest on recall-based interviews and a catchment indicator table [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1].

mitigation_mechanism: When rainfall is erratic, stone bunds conserve more moisture in the soil and ease crop water stress during dry spells, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. Rwandan land-husbandry project households showed greater resilience than controls to the 2016 drought and recovered faster, and the WOCAT compiler for orchard terraces in Uzbekistan rates drought impacts as reduced, noting that more water is captured and infiltrated, making the land less susceptible to droughts [ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts]. A terracing study citing De Graaff (2005) states that terracing reduces the risk of crop failure during dry spells in the rainy season through its water-conserving effect [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13].
caveats: Stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield benefit in the driest year (1985) and so did not reduce famine risk then, which bounds the cited dry-year gain [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. The Rwandan finding comes from a bundled package whose terrace share is unknown, and the Uzbek unit is a compiler rating rather than a measurement [ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts].

mitigation_mechanism: In-field practices let more rain infiltrate and hold water in the soil, so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï pits gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year on degraded land that otherwise yielded nothing, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. The zaï and stone-bund yield figures come from one study, Kaboré and Reij, the stone-bund figure as restated by Zougmoré and colleagues, so they are not independent confirmations [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. In Malawi's El Niño drought season ground cover (a soil-cover mulch, modelled separately from the other practices) raised maize from 247 kg per hectare on control plots to 432 kg per hectare and raised the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement [ev_crop_yield_boil19_2, ev_food_security_boil19_1]. Storage works carry water into dry periods: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells, rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss in critical drought periods, pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, WOCAT compilers in Burkina Faso, Cambodia, Somalia and Uzbekistan rate drought impacts as reduced, and in a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. Chololo pits in Tanzania are reported to mitigate drought effects [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_7]. Physical soil and water conservation structures were reported to buffer crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm and 1-m half-moon plots mitigated the impact of dry spells by retaining moisture for 2-3 weeks [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. mitigation_mechanism: Zaï and tassa pits increase infiltration and the water retention capacity of the soil, so crops suffer less from drought spells at the onset of and during the rainy season [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In rainfall-deficit periods zaï allowed cereals to be grown on degraded crusted soils in Burkina Faso, gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year where untreated land yielded nothing, and only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger [ev_crop_yield_roose93_3, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s]. In Malawi's El Niño drought season ground cover (a soil-cover mulch, modelled separately from the other practices) raised maize from 247 kg per hectare on control plots to 432 kg per hectare and raised the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement [ev_crop_yield_boil19_2, ev_food_security_boil19_1]. Chololo pits in Tanzania are reported to mitigate drought effects [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_7]. Farmers practising basins in Zambia, Zimbabwe and Limpopo reported maize and sorghum yields of >1 tonnes per hectare even in seasons with poor rainfall (<450 mm), against total crop failure under conventional ploughing [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. In a Zimbabwe household panel, conservation agriculture (mostly planting basins, with residue mulch and rotation on some plots) improved maize yields during times of drought, and sorghum and cowpea yields too [ev_crop_yield_mich19_3, ev_crop_yield_mich19_5]. In Nigeria, tied ridging with wood-shavings mulch raised sorghum grain yield over the flat bed by 67% in 1999 [ev_crop_yield_chir06_6], and in Malawi maize under conservation agriculture produced 700 kg per hectare more grain than conventional practice in 2015/16 [ev_crop_yield_seti18_1].
caveats: Zaï only reduces the impact of a dry spell of two to three weeks, and only where soil water storage capacity is at least 50 mm, so it does not address seasonal drought [ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In Mozambique no cowpea yield was obtained on any treatment in a season heavily affected by drought [ev_crop_yield_thierf15_2]. The Malawi on-farm survey of ground cover gives measured support, while the zaï and tassa yield contrasts are author estimates [ev_crop_yield_boil19_2, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s]. Not every in-field practice helped in that Malawi El Nino season: banking, the reinforcement of ridges while the crop is growing, cut maize from 245 to 153 kg per hectare and lowered the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054 [ev_crop_yield_boil19_5, ev_food_security_boil19_3]. In the Zimbabwe panel conservation agriculture had no specific impact in mitigating rainfall-shortfall losses for millet and groundnut [ev_crop_yield_mich19_6]. The farmer-reported basin yields compare fertilised basins with unfertilised ploughing, which the author warns makes those datasets too confounded [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. mitigation_mechanism: Stored runoff applied as supplemental irrigation is where the largest drought-season gains are measured. Runoff-fed storage carries water into dry periods: pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns catching runoff on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and a review of small reservoirs counts improved drought resilience among their cited benefits [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1]. WOCAT compilers for a pond in Cambodia and check dams in Somalia rate drought impacts as reduced, the Cambodian sheet noting the pond provides enough water even during drought and the Somali sheet crediting improved soil moisture retention and infiltration [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. Stored water bridges dry spells: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, and rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss in critical drought periods [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2]. In a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. In a Burkina Faso farm-pond trial, sorghum given supplemental irrigation from the harvested runoff yielded 680 against 443 kg per hectare in 1999 and 1138 against 634 kg per hectare in 2000, both seasons with serious dry spells [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_4, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_5]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial (Barron and Okwach), supplemental irrigation from a runoff-fed earth dam plus fertiliser raised maize yields over fertilised plots without irrigation in low-rainfall seasons (<300 mm) but not in seasons above 300 mm, and in a dry long-rains season only the irrigated plots produced any grain at all [ev_crop_yield_barr05_3, ev_crop_yield_barr05_4]. A risk model of a Burkina Faso farm reservoir, built on field experience, finds all mild dry spells mitigated by supplemental irrigation and severe late dry spells reduced to mild ones [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_7, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. A watershed model of the Arvari in Rajasthan (Glendenning and Vervoort 2011, cited in a review) found rainwater harvesting gave a slight buffer in drought years through more reliable groundwater stores, despite reducing streamflow [ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6]. A survey and modelling study in semi-arid Zimbabwe (Kahinda et al. 2007, cited in a review) found rainwater irrigation from macro-catchments raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre by mitigating intra-seasonal dry spells [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5].
caveats: The gains hold for dry spells within a season, not for a failed season: where the catchment produces no runoff the store has nothing to give. Storage is exhausted in prolonged drought: Brazilian subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long droughts, a benefit shortfall rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The Loess Plateau claim is a qualitative assertion, the reservoir finding a vote count and the Brazilian pond statement an institutional assertion without data, and the Cambodian and Somali units are compiler ratings [ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. The supplemental-irrigation and crop-loss statements are secondary citations in reviews, and the Kenyan sand-dam figures come from a catchment indicator table whose values are likely interview-derived [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. In the Kenyan dam trial's drought season the catchment yielded no runoff to irrigate with, both biomass and grain were strongly hit by the lack of water, and no treatment differed from another [ev_crop_yield_barr05_5]. The Burkina Faso reservoir model marks the limit: a meteorological drought cannot be mitigated because there is too little water to harvest, and severe late dry spells at flowering and grain filling are only partly mitigated because the reservoir supports two supplemental irrigations where at least three are needed [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_5, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. The zaï and stone-bund yield figures come from one study, Kaboré and Reij, the stone-bund figure as restated by Zougmoré and colleagues, so they are not independent confirmations [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers obtained 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 368 kg on conventional plots in the 2006/07 season, which the source calls a drought year [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 2.53 against 1.82 t per hectare without inputs (not significant) and 4.10 against 3.15 t per hectare with manure and fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the dry spells of the season [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. caveats: The storage pool still rests largely on compiler ratings, programme assertions and surveys, and includes the subsurface dams in Brazil that dried out in a rainless year [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1]. The benefit shrinks in severe drought: stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year (1985), Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, and zaï only buffers a dry spell of two to three weeks [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. Storage also runs out, with subsurface dams in Brazil drying out in a rainless year and consecutive drought years in Tunisia limiting soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. The Ethiopian dry-spell finding is a field observation of which plots wilted, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. Water harvesting is not irrigation, and the new primaries mark the limit: at the more arid Kenyan sites of Laikipia and Machakos each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, with 0 kg per hectare of maize harvested at Machakos due to meteorological drought, and the conservation-farming treatments did not avert it [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. The East African low-rainfall gain is for the best system per site, ripping or pitting usually with fertiliser, so it is bundled with reduced tillage and fertiliser, and the authors read it as a trend from their own figure [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The Zimbabwe water-productivity gain and the Rajasthan drought buffer are modelling results cited second-hand [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6].

mitigation_mechanism: A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia found significantly higher yield improvements in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter years, and yield gains also in below-average rainfall years, though not significant there [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. In semi-arid Brazil, water from small earth reservoirs applied as supplemental irrigation during the dry spells that commonly interrupt the rainy season has reduced farming risk in years of irregular rainfall, so the crop does not suffer water stress or die [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. Water stored in production cisterns can serve to reduce animal deaths in periods of more severe drought, which matters to semi-arid farm families because small herds are a key household asset [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths, as easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. Adgo et al. cite Posthumus and De Graaff (2005), a Peruvian bench-terrace study, for terracing reducing the risk of crop failure during rainy-season dry spells through its water-conserving effect [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13].
caveats: Storage runs out in long droughts: subsurface dams at Mutuca (Pesqueira) tended to dry up through 2001, a year without rain, and at Ouricuri the small dams do not withstand long droughts, so fruit availability depends on the length and intensity of each year's rains; these units record no benefit at that point rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The meta-analysis compares drier against average rainfall years and pools in-soil and reservoir techniques; its China-dominated sample sets this upper-middle-income scope while its African sub-sample is lower income, and many of its observations also carried soil fertility treatment, which the authors control for [ev_crop_yield_boum16_3, ev_crop_yield_boum16_4]. The Peruvian terrace finding is a secondary citation [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13]. The Brazilian benefit units are institutional statements without data: the Embrapa passages assess technologies the institute itself promotes, with no measured drought contrast or normal-year reference, and the cistern passage describes a potential effect, while the dry-up findings come from field observation and interviews with a few families [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3].

justification.statement: water_harvesting_conservation reduces the impact of drought (strength not quantified in the evidence) in semi_arid (upper_middle income contexts); the measured evidence also includes no-benefit or reversal results under drought, which discount the class; at severe or extreme drought the measured results show no benefit (it is not a defence against late-onset or extreme drought) (robust evidence, high agreement → very_high confidence; transfer: in_context). justification.mechanism: A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia found significantly higher yield improvements in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter years, and yield gains also in below-average rainfall years, though not significant there [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. In semi-arid Brazil, water from small earth reservoirs applied as supplemental irrigation during the dry spells that commonly interrupt the rainy season has reduced farming risk in years of irregular rainfall, so the crop does not suffer water stress or die [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. Water stored in production cisterns can serve to reduce animal deaths in periods of more severe drought, which matters to semi-arid farm families because small herds are a key household asset [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths, as easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. Adgo et al. cite Posthumus and De Graaff (2005), a Peruvian bench-terrace study, for terracing reducing the risk of crop failure during rainy-season dry spells through its water-conserving effect [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13].
justification.conditionality: Storage runs out in long droughts: subsurface dams at Mutuca (Pesqueira) tended to dry up through 2001, a year without rain, and at Ouricuri the small dams do not withstand long droughts, so fruit availability depends on the length and intensity of each year's rains; these units record no benefit at that point rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The meta-analysis compares drier against average rainfall years and pools in-soil and reservoir techniques; its China-dominated sample sets this upper-middle-income scope while its African sub-sample is lower income, and many of its observations also carried soil fertility treatment, which the authors control for [ev_crop_yield_boum16_3, ev_crop_yield_boum16_4]. The Peruvian terrace finding is a secondary citation [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13]. The Brazilian benefit units are institutional statements without data: the Embrapa passages assess technologies the institute itself promotes, with no measured drought contrast or normal-year reference, and the cistern passage describes a potential effect, while the dry-up findings come from field observation and interviews with a few families [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3].

mitigation_mechanism: In mixed crop–livestock settings the evidence is the same as for rainfed cropping, with an Ethiopian watershed programme evaluation added. These are programme-scale or unspecified soil and water conservation packages. A review of impact studies finds such methods particularly useful in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability, Ethiopia's PSNP public works improved watershed drought resilience by increasing water availability, and in semi-arid Brazil production cisterns can reduce animal mortality in severe drought [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. Physical soil and water conservation structures were also reported to buffer crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia, and a water-harvesting review states that dry spells can be bridged through investments in water management [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia (Bouma and colleagues) found significantly larger yield improvements in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter years, and gains in below-average rainfall years that were higher but not significant [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. In Ethiopia, the Sustainable Land Management Programme reduced vulnerability to severe drought in treated watersheds against control watersheds, with programme effects three times larger where severe droughts occurred, and buffered moderate droughts significantly on both vegetation measures used [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2].
caveats: The same review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought and different coping mechanisms are required [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. The PSNP note adds that vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, and in Tunisia four consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. Apart from the water-harvesting meta-analysis, every unit is a bundled programme, pooled soil and water conservation or an expert review, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated; the Brazilian statement describes potential without data and the Ethiopian 2015 finding is a secondary citation [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]. The Ethiopian programme result is measured on remotely sensed vegetation greenness and productivity rather than crop yields, comes from a programme that bundles surface water harvesting with small-scale irrigation, gully rehabilitation, grazing control and reforestation, and under mild drought the buffering showed on the greenness index but not on the productivity measure [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4].

mitigation_mechanism: Zaï and tassa pits increase infiltration and the water retention capacity of the soil, so crops suffer less from drought spells at the onset of and during the rainy season [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In rainfall-deficit periods zaï allowed cereals to be grown on degraded crusted soils in Burkina Faso, gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year where untreated land yielded nothing, and only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger [ev_crop_yield_roose93_3, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s]. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers obtained 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 368 kg on conventional plots in the 2006/07 season, which the source calls a drought year [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 2.53 against 1.82 t per hectare without inputs (not significant) and 4.10 against 3.15 t per hectare with manure and fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3]. Chololo pits in Tanzania are reported to mitigate drought effects [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_7]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the contrast was 1520 against 400 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_2]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the dry spells of the season [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. In on-farm conservation-farming trials in Kenya, Tanzania and Ethiopia the largest yield difference over conventional ploughing came in rainy seasons with low rainfall, when the practice maximises rainfall infiltration so the crop can bridge short periods of dry spell [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. In Zambia's 2001/2 season of very scattered rainfall, maize in hand-hoe conservation-farming basins yielded 3,054 kg per hectare against 1,339 kg under ploughing, which the authors say showcased the water-harvesting benefits of the basins [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1].
caveats: Zaï only reduces the impact of a dry spell of two to three weeks, and only where soil water storage capacity is at least 50 mm [ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In the Kenyan trial's short rains with meteorological droughts, tied ridging gave no advantage (0.52 against 0.53 t per hectare without inputs, 1.17 against 1.27 with manure and fertiliser) because there was little or no rainwater to hold in the basins [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5, ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]. The zaï and tassa contrasts are author estimates, the Zimbabwe planting-basin gain also carries manure and fertiliser, and the Kenyan tied-ridging result comes from a single-site trial [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1]. The Ethiopian dry-spell finding is a field observation of which plots wilted, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. Water harvesting is not irrigation, and the new primaries mark the limit: at the more arid Kenyan sites of Laikipia and Machakos each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, with 0 kg per hectare of maize harvested at Machakos due to meteorological drought, and the conservation-farming treatments did not avert it [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. The East African low-rainfall gain is for the best system per site, ripping or pitting usually with fertiliser, so it is bundled with reduced tillage and fertiliser, and the authors read it as a trend from their own figure [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. The Zambia 2001/2 basin contrast is a raw comparison in a single season with no normal-year reference, and most basin farmers received hybrid seed, fertiliser and lime on credit, so part of the gap is the input package [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1].

mitigation_mechanism: Runoff-fed storage carries water into dry periods: pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns catching runoff on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and a review of small reservoirs counts improved drought resilience among their cited benefits [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1]. WOCAT compilers for a pond in Cambodia and check dams in Somalia rate drought impacts as reduced, the Cambodian sheet noting the pond provides enough water even during drought and the Somali sheet crediting improved soil moisture retention and infiltration [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. Stored water bridges dry spells: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, and rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss in critical drought periods [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2]. Indian farmers reported a 6% chance of rainy-season crop failure from aberrant rains with a farm pond against 20% in the same crop–tree–livestock system without a pond [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1]. In Zimbabwe the months water could be collected at sand-dam sites in a drought year rose from 5.8 before construction to 9.7 after [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths, as easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. Stored runoff used as irrigation raises the return on scarce water: a survey and modelling study in semi-arid Zimbabwe, cited by Biazin et al., found that rainwater irrigation from macro-catchments raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre by mitigating intra-seasonal dry spells (Kahinda et al., 2007), and a conceptual watershed model for Rajasthan showed that rainwater harvesting structures recharging groundwater gave a slight buffer in drought years (Glendenning and Vervoort, 2011, cited by Glendenning et al.) [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6].
caveats: Storage is exhausted in prolonged drought: Brazilian subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long droughts, a benefit shortfall rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The Loess Plateau claim is a qualitative assertion, the reservoir finding a vote count and the Brazilian pond statement an institutional assertion without data, and the Cambodian and Somali units are compiler ratings [ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. The supplemental-irrigation and crop-loss statements are secondary citations in reviews, the Indian pond figures come from a farmer survey reported in a preprint, and the Zimbabwe sand-dam figure rests on recall-based before-and-after interviews [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The Zimbabwe and Rajasthan findings are modelling results cited second-hand, and the Rajasthan model also showed the structures reducing streamflow, a downstream cost of the same recharge [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6].

mitigation_mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and infiltration trenches slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces lowered mean runoff and flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower peak discharges at the foot of the slope, trenches significantly reduced plot runoff across the reviewed studies, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment reduced flood runoff volume, clipped peaks and lengthened flood duration [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage during the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Spate and diversion structures in Yemen are reported to control floods, users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive flood limitation as a benefit, compacted hill terraces in Uttarakhand, India are credited with limiting flood and landslide damage, and in heavy rain stone bunds protect land in Burkina Faso from rapid flow [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_2]. WOCAT compilers in Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Tunisia and Uzbekistan rate flooding as reduced and say how: rain retained where it falls, a dam or series of dams acting as a downstream buffer, stone lines and walls cutting peak flows, and structures slowing runoff velocity [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts]. Embrapa credits its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, with easing floods as well [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
caveats: The sub-practices disagree, and the split runs through terracing: bunds and terraces that slow and spread runoff on the slope lowered peak discharges, while structures that divert runoff did the opposite — diversion banquettes in Niger raised peak discharges and runoff-diversion systems accelerate concentration time, with serious gully risk if the dikes break [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. In-situ, runoff-catchment and spate rows each show a moderate reduction on their own, so whether the practice eases or worsens flooding depends on whether it holds water in place or concentrates it. Storage size matters too: larger sand dams increase flooding risk, and a check-dam review finds a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where structures were ill-designed and not maintained [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. Catchment-level terrace evidence is scarce, most measured results are at plot or hillslope scale, the Tunisian catchment result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, and the Italian check-dam cases are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting rather than farm water harvesting [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. The barraginha flood statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, unmeasured, and a landscape-scale effect rather than one on the adopting farm [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

mitigation_mechanism: Practices that hold water on the cropped field backfire in wet conditions: in wet years stone bunds in Burkina Faso may cause waterlogging in some parts of the field, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the Sudanian zone of Cameroon, where rainfall exceeds 1 200 mm per year, sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial waterlogging lasting 3–5 days during early maize growth also affected the mulching and basin treatments [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. In southern Africa an FAO study shows by a water-balance calculation that planting basins can depress yields when too much water concentrates in them under high rainfall or in seasons with abnormally high rainfall, and concludes that in sub-humid environments yields could be affected by water-logging in years with adequate rainfall [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8, ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial, ridged plots with fertiliser at the relatively wetter sub-humid Rachuonyo site gave the lowest yields, slightly below conventional practice, which the authors say can probably be explained by waterlogging caused by ridging [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6]. Biazin et al. cite Jensen et al. (2003) from Tanzania: tied ridges helped maize in years of near-normal (500–600 mm) rainfall, but in wet years (700–900 mm) the maize showed waterlogging effects [ev_waterlogging_hazard_biaz12_15].
caveats: Every unit in the row points the same way, so the practice is rated as worsening waterlogging, but none states how large the loss is or what share of a field is affected, so the strength is not quantified. The harm is tied to wet years, high-rainfall zones or sub-humid sites: it comes from using in-field water-holding practices (pits, basins, mulch, ridges, stone bunds) outside their rainfall window, and says nothing about storage or diversion structures, which have no waterlogging evidence left in this row. The Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors, and the Burkina Faso statements and the Tanzanian tied-ridge result are cited from earlier studies [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_biaz12_15]. The Ethiopian finding is a field observation with no measured yield loss, and the source names a tillage treatment as the one particularly affected, so only part of the harm can be put on mulch and basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. The southern African basin finding rests on a theoretical water balance plus extension reports and farmer testimony, and the sub-humid conclusion covers conservation agriculture bundled with reduced tillage [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8, ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. The Kenyan ridging loss is the authors' probable explanation rather than a measured waterlogging contrast, and the ridging is bundled with fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6]. The Cameroon, Burkina Faso and Kenyan losses are held out of the production classes as performance caveats and counted here as waterlogging evidence.

mitigation_mechanism: Intense runoff overwhelms or breaks structures: floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, check-dam failure releases stored sediment, large floods could wash out traditional spate diversions in Yemen, banquettes lack capacity for erosive rains and overflow, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. On China's Loess Plateau, sediment-filled check dams are vulnerable to large floods: more than 200 mm of rain falling on 26 July 2017 in Suide and Zizhou counties produced a flood that damaged 20% of the main check dams [ev_climate_shock_shi19_3]. A check-dam review cites structural failure from the impact of large boulders in extreme floods, and grassed earth gully check dams in Morocco are described as fragile during major floods and needing frequent winter maintenance [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1_av, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge jessour in Tunisia, zaï pits, bunds and trenches in Niger, the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, check dam ponds in Ethiopia, radical terraces in Rwanda, and gully-plugging check dams in Nepal not to cope well with river or flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1616_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1528_2012_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1547_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1493_2011_general_river_flood].
caveats: Other compilers judge sand dams in Kenya, check dams in Tunisia, China and India, and spate or water-spreading systems in Eritrea and Sudan to cope well, those for marab and Vallerani systems in Jordan and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia to cope very well, and those for weirs in Ethiopia and works in Somalia to cope moderately [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1537_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6716_2023_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7777_2026_flash_flood]; these are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, and for field-level practices (pits, bunds, trenches) a not-well rating describes exposure of fields to floodwater rather than damage to a structure. justification.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: both units come from one technology sheet and are practitioner ratings, with no observed damage or fire event described, and coping moderately itself implies some damage [ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_forest_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_land_fire]. mitigation_mechanism: Reservoirs, tanks and dams trap the sediment that runoff carries, so storage fills and function declines: Tigray dams with a 30-year design life were set to run their cycle in 4.4 to 5.7 years, eight of ten Zambian reservoirs lost storage to siltation, 31 percent of earthen dams in Haryana silted up within five years, Moroccan gabions had nearly lost their original function, and small hill dams in Morocco lose 0.5 to 1% of capacity each year to catchment erosion [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1, ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. Loose-rock check dams on semi-arid rangeland watersheds in the USA were filled to more than 80% of capacity within four years, and a review notes the sediment-control effect of check dams diminishes as they fill and becomes marginal a few years to a few decades after installation [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1_av]. In Tigray, Gebremeskel et al. cite Berhane et al. (2016) for siltation threatening the benefits of 61% of surveyed micro-dams, ahead of leakage and structural damage [ev_climate_shock_gebr18_5]. On China's Loess Plateau high sediment loads fill check dams rapidly, so their trapping gives only short-term erosion-control benefit [ev_climate_shock_shi19_4]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime, and an Indian review cites Gunnell and Krishnamurthy (2003) that all rainwater-harvesting structures need regular silt clearing to stay functional and maximise recharge [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_11_av]. On Ethiopian highland bunds, a filled drainage ditch quickly lowers sediment-trapping efficiency and adds pressure that can lead to structural failure [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av]. In Burkina Faso the 2- and 3-m half-moon plots showed lower infiltration than the control plots, likely due to suspended matter that clogs the soil during sedimentation [ev_soil_permeability_zour25h1_8].
caveats: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units, including the Tigray and Indian maintenance statements, are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, the only directly measured fill rate comes from a high-income rangeland study, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place and small hill dams were forgotten once built [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_climate_shock_gebr18_5, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_11_av, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. The half-moon clogging is a loss of infiltration in the larger basins, with a likely cause the authors name but do not test, not a structural failure [ev_soil_permeability_zour25h1_8].

mitigation_mechanism: On Ethiopian soil and water conservation structures, a review reports second-hand that when the drainage ditch behind a structure fills with sediment, trapping efficiency quickly decreases and the extra pressure on the structure can lead to structural failure [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av].
caveats: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single statement cited second-hand in a review, with no rate or frequency of failure; it does describe a damage pathway, and implies the damage depends on whether ditches are cleared [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding on how often silted structures fail.

Loose-rock check dams on semi-arid rangeland watersheds in the USA were filled to more than 80% of capacity within four years, and a review notes the sediment-control effect of check dams diminishes as they fill and becomes marginal a few years to a few decades after installation [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1_av]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1]. In Tigray, a survey cited in a review (Berhane et al. 2016) found siltation threatening the benefits of 61% of water-harvesting structures, ahead of leakage and structural damage [ev_climate_shock_gebr18_5]; on China's Loess Plateau high sediment loads fill check dams rapidly, so trapping gives only short-term erosion-control benefit [ev_climate_shock_shi19_4]; and in India rainwater-harvesting structures need regular clearing of accumulated silt to stay functional and maximise recharge (Gunnell and Krishnamurthy 2003, cited in a review) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_11_av].
caveats: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, the only directly measured fill rate comes from a high-income rangeland study, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place and small hill dams were forgotten once built [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. mitigation_mechanism: Storms overtop, breach or collapse works: storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau, with few local funds to repair it, staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of rains below 50 mm, but in the biggest storms the excess overtops the bunds and gullies the slope, tied ridges in a Kenyan trial collapsed in heavy rainfall events and had to be rebuilt within the season, and poorly structured vineyard terraces in Spain suffered severe landslides after a single rainstorm [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_climate_shock_roos10_1_av, ev_climate_shock_ndun23_1_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av]. In Algeria a poorly maintained banquette network fails in a chain reaction during torrential and prolonged rains, the smallest unrepaired breach spreading sliding through the whole network [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av], and a check-dam review links failures worldwide to extreme rainfall events or lack of maintenance [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge zaï pits, contour stone bunds, semi-circular bunds, contour bunds and Vallerani trenches in Niger, radical terraces in Rwanda, stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde, and gully-plugging check dams in Nepal not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1219_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1616_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1614_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1652_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1613_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm]. A review of farming terraces adds that soil saturation in very heavy storms, or runoff accumulating behind the walls, is a determining factor in the failure and movement of terrace risers, and that with heavy rainfall shallow terrace landslides can become debris flows that affect the entire terraced hillside [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av, ev_climate_shock_arna15_9_av].

mitigation_mechanism: Storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau, with few local funds to repair it, poorly structured vineyard terraces in Spain suffered severe landslides after a single rainstorm, and in Algeria a poorly maintained banquette network fails in a chain reaction during torrential and prolonged rains, the smallest unrepaired breach spreading sliding through the whole network [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge radical terraces in Rwanda, stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and contour stone bunds in Niger not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1616_2014_local_rainstorm]. A review of terraced landscapes describes the mechanism: soil saturation on terraces in very heavy storms, or runoff accumulating behind the walls, is a determining factor in the failure and movement of terrace risers, and under heavy rainfall landslides normally confined to small parts of a terrace can become debris flows across the whole terraced hillside [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av, ev_climate_shock_arna15_9_av].
caveats: Other compilers judge progressive bench terraces in China, stone-covered bench terraces in Yemen, stone lines in Uganda, vetiver-hedge terraces in Haiti and bench terraces in Bangladesh to cope well with rainstorms, and a continuous bench terrace for tea in Thailand to cope very well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1522_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1560_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1589_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm]; thunderstorms are rated as coping moderately for Bangladesh terraces and vegetated stone bunds in Burkina Faso, while Bangladesh terraces cope very well with hailstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6729_2023_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_hailstorm]. Damage in the literature follows poor construction or maintenance (poorly structured terraces in Spain, poorly maintained banquettes in Algeria) and the Loess Plateau evaluation gives no measure of damage, so apart from the terrace review the rest of the evidence is compiler ratings [ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av, ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av, ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7]. The review statements describe how failure happens, not how often, and give no magnitude [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av, ev_climate_shock_arna15_9_av].

The damage figures are secondary citations tied to marl and clay substrates and to abandonment rather than to maintained terraces, and the ratings are practitioner judgements [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av].
